_meta.districts_note: Chhattisgarh has 33 districts in 5 revenue divisions (Raipur 5, Durg 7, Bilaspur 8, Surguja 6, Bastar 7; division membership per Wikipedia 'List of districts of Chhattisgarh'). History: 16 districts at statehood (1 Nov 2000); Bijapur and Narayanpur added 11 May 2007 (18 = the Census 2011 frame); 9 districts from 1 Jan 2012 (Sukma, Kondagaon, Balod, Bemetara, Baloda Bazar-Bhatapara, Gariaband, Mungeli, Surajpur, Balrampur-Ramanujganj) = 27; Gaurela-Pendra-Marwahi inaugurated 10 Feb 2020 = 28; Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki (2 Sep 2022), Sarangarh-Bilaigarh and Khairagarh-Chhuikhadan-Gandai (3 Sep 2022), Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur and Sakti (9 Sep 2022) = 33. Parents: MCB from Koriya; MMAC and KCG from Rajnandgaon; Sarangarh-Bilaigarh from Raigarh (Sarangarh, Baramkela) + Baloda Bazar-Bhatapara (Bilaigarh, Bhatgaon); Sakti from Janjgir-Champa; GPM from Bilaspur. 'population_2011' on each district is an exact re-aggregation of Census 2011 village/town units into the LGD 2023 polygons (see the census file); 'population_2011_des_cg' is the figure the Chhattisgarh Directorate of Economics & Statistics published (Socio Economic Indicator 2015, via Wikipedia) where available - they differ by up to ~7% for Sukma/Bastar and Koriya/MCB because of boundary vintages.
_meta.coordinates_note: District and taluka centroids are area centroids computed in EPSG:32644 from the LGD district/sub-district polygons (ramSeraph/indian_admin_boundaries, Dec 2023) after fixing the LGD mislabel of Nawagarh sub-district 03311 (moved from Janjgir-Champa to Bemetara). Town points: Wikipedia article coordinates when the point lies inside (or within 3 km of) the town's current-district polygon; otherwise OpenStreetMap Nominatim place nodes (tahsil-boundary centroids rejected); a handful are flagged 'approximate' (nearest named OSM feature such as a railway station or health centre); null when nothing verifiable was found. Many Wikipedia coordinates are 2-decimal (~1 km). Every coordinate was checked against its district polygon; exceptions carry coord_note.
_meta.devanagari_note: Town Devanagari aliases are the titles of the linked Hindi Wikipedia articles (suffixes like ', छत्तीसगढ़' stripped), or Wikidata Hindi labels (Jamul, Nagri, Kirodimal Nagar). For towns listed in devanagari_manual there was no Hindi Wikipedia/Wikidata label and the Devanagari was written by hand (standard Hindi-press spellings) - verify before using for exact-match search. All villages_and_localities Devanagari aliases are hand-written. District 'hindi' values come from Hindi Wikipedia district titles ('जिला' removed); four multi-part names (Baloda Bazar-Bhatapara, Balrampur-Ramanujganj, MCB, MMAC) are composed and flagged with hindi_note.
_meta.talukas_note: talukas = the 164 sub-district polygons in the LGD Dec-2023 layer (163 named + one unnamed 'Katghora-1'). This is every district-HQ tehsil and all 2011 tehsils, plus 15 post-2011 tehsils that had polygons (e.g. Chirmiri, Kelhari, Kotadol, Gandai, Salhewara, Khadgaon, Aundhi, Adbhar, Baradwar, Hasaud, Bhatgaon, Sariya, Tongpal, Gadiras). Chhattisgarh has notified many more tehsils since 2019 (e.g. Koriya's Patna; well over 200 statewide) which are not in the layer and are not listed. hq is inferred from the tehsil name (LGD gives none). population_2011 = Census 2011 villages assigned by their point location + towns (by town coordinate, else by the 2011 sub-district), summing exactly to the state total 25,545,198.
_meta.towns_note: Covers all 14 municipal corporations (Raipur, Bhilai, Durg, Bilaspur, Korba, Rajnandgaon, Raigarh, Jagdalpur, Ambikapur, Chirmiri, Dhamtari, Bhilai-Charoda, Birgaon, Risali), Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar), every district HQ, and ~110 other municipalities/nagar panchayats/tehsil towns. 'type' gives the role plus the Census 2011 civic status; statuses may have changed since (several NPs were upgraded, Tifra/Sirgitti/Bodri merged into Bilaspur MC in 2019, Risali split from Bhilai in 2019). population_2011 is the Census 2011 PCA town total (all parts summed, incl. outgrowths where the census reports 'M Corp. + OG'); null for places that were not separate towns in 2011.
_meta.villages_note: villages_and_localities = 159 politically salient places chosen by hand: Raipur/Bhilai/Bilaspur/Korba urban localities, industrial and mining areas (Siltara, Urla, Bhilai Steel Plant, Gevra, Kusmunda, Nagarnar, Bailadila, Raoghat, Gare-Pelma), Hasdeo Arand villages, Maoist-affected Bastar-division villages and incident sites (Silger, Tadmetla, Burkapal, Minpa, Tarrem/Tekalguda, Aranpur, Sarkeguda, Edesmetta, Jhiram Ghati, Chhotebethiya, Thulthuli, Puvarti, Abujhmarh villages), tribal-block HQs, and religious/heritage sites (Giraudpuri, Sirpur, Bhoramdeo). district = current district. Coordinates: Wikipedia, then Census 2011 village points (ramSeraph Census_Villages; population_2011 from the same row), then Survey of India village points (Bastar only), then Nominatim. Where several same-name census villages exist in a district the most populous was used (flagged in coord_source). Urban locality points are often approximate (a named OSM feature inside the locality).

centroid.source: Area centroid (EPSG:32644) of the LGD Chhattisgarh state polygon (ramSeraph/indian_admin_boundaries, LGD_States.parquet, Dec 2023).

bbox.source: Bounds of the LGD Chhattisgarh state polygon; the HindustanTimesLabs chhattisgarh_AC.json bounds agree within 0.01 deg (17.7828-24.1056 N, 80.2446-84.3960 E).

geojson_sources.what: AC boundaries (Chhattisgarh only, GeoJSON) - use for the 90-AC map layer
geojson_sources.license: MIT (repository licence, github.com/HindustanTimesLabs/shapefiles); folder README gives no source or delimitation info
geojson_sources.notes: Checked 2026-09-26 (GitHub contents API + download): HTTP 200, 482,314 bytes, EPSG:4326 (no crs member), exactly 90 features, AC_NO 1-90 each once (no AC_NO 0 sliver, unlike Goa). Geometry types Polygon + GeometryCollection (flatten GeometryCollection to MultiPolygon as in build_goa_geojson.js). Properties: AC_NO (string "1".."90"), AC_NAME (e.g. "Ramanujganj (ST)", "Raipur City North", "Durg-Rural", "Mohla-Manpur (ST)"; one truncated value: AC 1 = "Bharatpur-Sonhat (S" -> "Bharatpur-Sonhat (ST)"), PC_NO, PC_NAME (e.g. "SURGUJA (ST)", "JANJGIR-CHAMPA (SC" truncated), PC_ID (2201..2211), DIST_NAME (16 pre-2012 districts with stray '*' and typos, e.g. "BASTER", "KAWARDHA *", "DANTEWADA*" - do NOT use for current districts), DT_CODE, ST_CODE "22", ST_NAME "CHHATTISGARH", plus styling keys stroke/stroke-opacity/fill-opacity/visibility and Shape_Leng/Shape_Area/MaxSimpTol/MinSimpTol. POST-2008 delimitation (names include Marwahi, Beltara, Bhatgaon, Premnagar, Vaishali Nagar, Raipur City West/North/South, Sanjari Balod, Mohla-Manpur, Chitrakot). Total area 135,141 km2 vs LGD state polygon 135,134 km2. Bounds 17.7828-24.1056 N, 80.2446-84.3960 E. Take AC names, reservation, current district and Lok Sabha seat from a voter-profile file rather than these attributes.

geojson_sources.what: AC boundaries (all-India shapefile, same ECI-derived geometry family)
geojson_sources.notes: Checked 2026-09-26: all four files HTTP 200 (shp 6.26 MB, dbf 5.72 MB). Chhattisgarh = 90 rows, ST_CODE 22, AC_NO 1-90, STATUS null.
